messages:
oliver: FYI the sample-app CI started failing on pyright and mypy after the latest SDK bump. root cause looks like autogenerated model typings. errors are mostly about Optional vs union syntax and a handful of `Any` creeping into return types.

sana: can you paste the concrete error? pyright output is usually more actionable.

oliver: pyright: `Expression of type "list[Item] | None" is not iterable` on a simple `for it in resp.items:`. mypy: `error: Item 1 has incompatible type "Any"; expected "Item"` on list literals created from parsing response.

lee: sounds like two separate emitter problems: (1) generator outputs runtime pydantic models but type-checkers can't see the fields (so they become Any), and (2) the generator emits modern `list[Foo] | None` which breaks consumers on older python or strict checker configs.

sana: proposal: emit explicit .pyi stubs next to generated modules. stubs should target py3.8+ and use `from typing import List, Optional, TYPE_CHECKING` and classical annotations. that should placate both mypy and pyright without changing runtime pydantic classes.

oliver: +1. Also, for streaming endpoints we should generate two overloads in pyi: one returning `AsyncIterator[bytes]` (raw) and another overload that, if `parse=True`, returns `AsyncIterator[ModelDelta]`. pyright respects overloads and will pick the right one based on the kwarg.

lee: good call. Example pyi snippet idea:
```python
from typing import AsyncIterator, overload
@overload
def stream_events(..., parse: bool = False) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]: ...
@overload
def stream_events(..., parse: bool = True) -> AsyncIterator[EventDelta]: ...
```

sana: edgecases: forward refs and circular models. stubs should use string literals for forward refs (e.g., `List["Foo"]`) and include `# type: ignore` for impossible resolves? I'd prefer `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports to avoid runtime imports in pyi.

oliver: also consider a tiny `redwood-types` package as an alternative: publish only pyi/types there so older SDK versions can depend on it for types. downside: more packaging. pyi-in-wheel is simpler.

ci-bot: CI failure: mypy check in sample-app (branch: oliver/pyi-stubs) 023-11-02 12:10:23 - see https://ci.redwood.example/build/1189

sana: I'll prototype adding `--emit-pyi` to the generator and a smoke test in the sample-app that runs both pyright and mypy. we'll also add `py.typed` to wheel if we include inline typing.

lee: one more gotcha: users who use `from __future__ import annotations` in their apps sometimes get mismatches between `list[Foo]` and `List["Foo"]`. stick with typing.List in stubs to minimise diffs. also document a migration note for users enabling `strict = True` in mypy.

oliver: cool. I'll open a draft PR with the stub emitter and the overloads for streaming functions. cc @sana for the pyi formatting rules. :rocket:
